texts.preamble: M/S Biswas & Sons vs The State Of Tripura on 7 October, 2025 High Court Of Tripura Agartala I.A. No.1 of 2025 in Wp(C) No.598 of 2025 M/S Biswas & Sons, a partnership firm,
texts.facts: The applicant-petitioner is a dealer of IOCL and the licence is granted by the authority in favour of IOCL. On the basis of lease agreement in between the predecessors of the petitioners and IOCL, the petitioners are/were running the outlet on behalf of IOCL at Motorstand, Agartala. But surprisingly all on a sudden the respondent No.3 issued Show Cause Notice on 23.09.2025 to the present applicant-petitioner. On receipt of Show Cause Notice, the applicant-petitioner appeared and sought time but the authority did not consider the same rather on the same day issued another notice to the present applicant-petitioner for hearing under Section 152 of BNSS (Annexure-4) and in response to that the applicant-petitioner submitted one prayer to respondent No.3 on 25.09.2025 to supply copies of the documents like written representation submitted by some of the local inhabitants of Old Motorstand, Agartala on 08.09.2025 and the report of Inquiry Committee consisting of Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar and Divisional Fire Officer, West Tripura, Agartala. But the respondent No.3 did not consider the same rather by order dated 26.09.2025 cancelled the No Objection Certificate which ought to have been issued to the original licensee i.e. IOCL but the respondent No.3 without communicating anything to the IOCL cancelled the No Objection Certificate and communicated the order on 26.09.2025 to the present applicant- petitioner. Learned Senior Counsel submitted that this retail outlet is the oldest outlet of the State and during the regime of Maharani this land was purchased and used for the purpose of retail outlet and earlier also the respondents-State did some arbitrary action and under compelling circumstances, the applicant-petitioner had to file one writ petition before this Court which was numbered as WP(C) No.206 of 2011 and after hearing, a coordinate bench of this High Court by order dated 09.09.2016 cancelled the arbitrary order of the respondent-State and till date no appeal has been preferred by the respondent-authority challenging the said judgment. Thus, the same has attained finality. It was further submitted that in view of Rule 150 of Petroleum Rules, 2002, the No Objection Certificate has been cancelled by the authority but from the contents of Show Cause Notice(Annexure-3) and Hearing Notice(Annexure-4), there would be no whisper that the same was cancelled in view of Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002. So, with an ulterior motive, the respondent No.3 has taken arbitrary action upon the petitioner and on the eve of Puja, their outlet has been closed resulting which the applicant-petitioner has sustained huge amount of financial losses and it is the only source of their earning
texts.arguments: It is further submitted by Learned Senior Counsel that the present applicant-petitioner is a partnership firm and engaged in the business of retail sale of petroleum products under Indian Oil Corporation Ltd.(AOD) having its outlet at Motorstand, Agartala, since 1938. and if at this stage, the arbitrary action is not stayed by an order of the Court till disposal of the Writ Petition then the petitioner would be seriously prejudiced and it would be harsh to them. On the other hand, Learned Advocate General appearing on behalf of the State-respondents No.1, 2 and 3 strongly countered the submission made by Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant-petitioner and submitted that this present writ petition is not maintainable and further submitted that the subject matter of WP(C) No.206 of 2011 is not similar to the present writ petition but the petitioner relying upon the said judgment is trying to make some cloud in the mind of the Court and on the basis of that judgment no relief can be granted in this case. It was further M/S Biswas & Sons vs The State Of Tripura on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85110784/ 2 submitted that based on the representation of some of the local inhabitants, an enquiry was conducted through Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Sadar and Divisional Fire Officer, West Tripura, Agartala and on the basis of their reports, No Objection Certificate was cancelled by respondent No.3 by cancellation order dated 26.09.2025 and there was no infirmity or perversity in the said order. It was further submitted by Learned Advocate General that considering the traffic movement and seriousness of the traffic congestion of that area, the respondent No.3 was compelled to issue Show Cause Notice from which it appears that the report of the Inquiring Authority was mentioned in the Show Cause Notice dated 23.09.2025(Annexure-3) and the findings of the Inquiring Authority was communicated to the present applicant- petitioner. So at this stage there is no scope to take the plea on their behalf that no report was furnished to them. In this regard, Learned Advocate General relied upon one citation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India Centre for Public Interest Litigation vs. Union of India & Ors., reported in (2013) 16 SCC 279 wherein in para No.25 and 26, Hon'ble the Apex Court observed as under: "25. We may emphasise that any food article which is hazardous or injurious to public health is a potential danger to the fundamental right to life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. A paramount duty is cast on the States and its authorities to achieve an appropriate level of protection to human life and health which is a fundamental right guaranteed to the citizens under Article 21 read with Article 47 of the Constitution of India. 26. We are, therefore, of the view that the provisions of the FSS Act and the PFA Act and the Rules and Regulations framed thereunder have to be interpreted and applied in the light of the constitutional principles discussed above and endeavour has to be made to achieve an appropriate level of protection of human life and health. Considerable responsibility is cast on the authorities as well as the other officers functioning under the abovementioned Acts to achieve the desired results. The authorities are also obliged to maintain a system of control and other activities as appropriate to the circumstances, including public communication on food safety and risk, food safety surveillance and other monitoring activities covering all stages of food business." Referring the same, Learned Advocate General drawn the attention of the Court that considering the public safety the order was issued by respondent No.3 and at this stage there is no scope to interfere with the said action of respondent No.3 (i.e. Annexure-6). On the other hand, Learned Senior Counsel Mr. Deb in course of hearing relied upon one citation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Gorkha Security Services vs. Government (NCT of Delhi) & Ors. reported in (2014) 9 SCC 105 wherein in para No.21, 22 and 26, Hon'ble the Apex Court observed as under: "Contents of the show-cause notice M/S Biswas & Sons vs The State Of Tripura on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85110784/ 3 21. Referring the same, Learned Senior Counsel drawn the attention of this Court that on bare perusal of Rule 150 and Rule 152 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, it would be clear as to under what circumstances the No Objection Certificate can be cancelled. Learned Counsel, Ms. Paramita Dhar appearing on behalf of IOCL admitted the case of the applicant-petitioner and submitted that nothing was communicated to the respondent No.4 by the respondent No.3 in taking some prompt action without affording opportunity to the present applicant-petitioner. Learned Counsel also admitted that the said respondent is the licensee and on the basis of lease agreement the present applicant-petitioner is running the outlet of the alleged petrol pump. (1) A no- objection certificate granted under rule 144 shall be liable to be cancelled by the District Authority or the State Government, if the District Authority or the State Government is satisfied, that the licensee has ceased to have any right to use the site for storing petroleum: Provided that before cancelling a no-objection certificate, the licensee shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. (2) A District Authority or a State Government cancelling a no-objection certificate shall record, in writing, the reasons for such cancellation and shall immediately furnish to the licensee and to the licensing authority concerned, copy of the order cancelling the no-objection certificate. 152. Suspension and cancellation of licence (1) Every licence granted under these rules shall- (i) stand cancelled, if the licensee ceases to have any right to the site for storing petroleum; M/S Biswas & Sons vs The State Of Tripura on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85110784/ 5 (ii) stand cancelled, if the no-objection certificate is cancelled by the District Authority or the State Government in accordance with sub-rule (1) of rule 150; (iii) be liable to be suspended or cancelled by an order of the licensing authority for any contravention of the Act or of any rule thereunder or of any condition contained in such licence, or by order of the Central Government, if it is satisfied that there are sufficient grounds for doing so: Provided that- (a) before suspending or cancelling a licence under this rule, the holder of the licence shall be given an opportunity of being heard; (b) the maximum period of suspension shall not exceed three months; and (c) the suspension of a licence shall not debar the holder of the licence from applying for its renewal in accordance with the provisions of rule 148. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (1), an opportunity of being heard may not be given to the holder of a licence before his licence is suspended or cancelled in cases- (a) where the licence is suspended by a licensing authority as an interim measure for violation of any of the provisions of the Act or these rules, or of any conditions contained in such licence and in his opinion such violations is likely to cause imminent danger to the public: Provided that where a licence is so suspended, the licensing authority shall give the holder of the licence an opportunity of being heard before the order of suspension is confirmed; or (b) where the licence is suspended or cancelled by the Central Government, if that Government considers that in the public interest or in the interest of the security of the State, such opportunity should not be given.
